title: Build a SOL Vault
description: Ship one small Anchor program that can hold SOL, enforce its authority, and survive adversarial tests.

stages.title: Create the vault
stages.promise: Give every authority one deterministic vault PDA.
stages.goal: Initialize a vault at the PDA derived from the fixed namespace `vault` and the authority public key.
contract: Use the exact seed formula: [b\"vault\", authority.key().as_ref()].
Store the authority, bump, and a zero tracked balance.
Only the authority pays for initialization.
stages.task: Finish the `initialize` instruction and its account constraints. Keep the starter program ID unchanged.
commonMistakes: Using a random keypair account instead of the PDA.
Leaving the bump or authority unset.
stages.delayedHint: The PDA constraint belongs on the vault account itself: initialize it with seeds, bump, and the authority as payer.

stages.title: Accept deposits
stages.promise: Move SOL in and keep an honest internal balance.
stages.goal: Transfer positive lamport amounts from the authority into the vault through the system program.
contract: Use a system-program CPI instead of mutating lamports directly.
Increase tracked balance with checked arithmetic.
stages.task: Implement `deposit(amount)` without changing the account interface in the starter.
commonMistakes: Updating tracked balance before the CPI succeeds.
stages.delayedHint: Build `system_program::Transfer { from: authority, to: vault }`, invoke it, then update `vault.tracked_balance`.

stages.title: Withdraw safely
stages.promise: Let the owner withdraw without turning the vault into a drain.
stages.goal: Allow the stored authority to withdraw a positive amount that the vault has actually tracked.
contract: Require the stored authority and the expected PDA.
Reject zero amounts and tracked-balance overdrafts.
Keep the vault rent-exempt after moving lamports.
stages.task: Implement `withdraw(amount)` with checked subtraction and an explicit rent-floor check.
commonMistakes: Checking only account lamports instead of tracked balance.
Letting the vault fall below its rent floor.
Moving SOL before validating every invariant.
stages.delayedHint: Validate `tracked_balance >= amount` first, calculate the rent floor from `Rent::get()`, then adjust both lamport balances only after all checks pass.

stages.title: Defend the vault
stages.promise: Make the happy path hard to abuse.
stages.goal: Tighten every validation boundary around deposit and withdrawal.
contract: Reject a wrong signer, wrong authority, wrong PDA, zero amount, and overdraft.
Use checked arithmetic for every stored balance update.
Preserve the vault rent floor on every successful withdrawal.
stages.task: Review the full program as an attacker would. Fix each validation gap without changing the public instruction interface.
commonMistakes: Relying on a single `has_one` check without PDA seeds.
Returning a generic panic instead of an Anchor error.
stages.delayedHint: Your account constraints should establish identity; handlers should establish amounts and lamport invariants. You need both layers.

stages.title: Close cleanly
stages.goal: Close an empty vault to its authority and reclaim its rent.
contract: Only the stored authority may close the vault.
Refuse to close if tracked balance is nonzero.
Use Anchor's close constraint to return account rent.
stages.task: Implement `close_vault` and ensure the state account can only be reclaimed after its recorded balance is zero.
commonMistakes: Closing a vault that still reports a balance.
Sending rent to an arbitrary recipient.
Removing PDA validation from the close context.
stages.delayedHint: Put `close = authority` in the account constraint and make `tracked_balance == 0` a handler requirement before returning Ok.
